# sysutils_group (Data Source)

Looks up an existing group in `/etc/group` by name or by gid. Exactly one of `name` and `gid` must be set; the other is filled in from the group that was found.

The group is read from `/etc/group`, the same file the [`sysutils_group`](../resources/group.md) resource manages, because that is where the member list is recorded. Groups provided only by directory services such as LDAP or SSSD are not found. The data source does not require root privileges.

A missing group is an error. The data source is read during planning, so a group that a [`sysutils_group`](../resources/group.md) resource in the same configuration creates is only found if the data source depends on that resource, for example through a reference to its `gid` or with `depends_on`.

## Example Usage

### Look up a group by name

```terraform
data "sysutils_group" "docker" {
  name = "docker"
}

output "docker_gid" {
  value = data.sysutils_group.docker.gid
}

output "docker_users" {
  value = data.sysutils_group.docker.members
}
```

### Look up a group by gid and add a member

```terraform
# Look up the group that owns /var/log files by gid ...
data "sysutils_group" "adm" {
  gid = 4
}

# ... and adopt it with one extra member, keeping the existing ones.
# Import it first with: terraform import sysutils_group.adm adm
resource "sysutils_group" "adm" {
  name    = data.sysutils_group.adm.name
  gid     = data.sysutils_group.adm.gid
  members = setunion(data.sysutils_group.adm.members, ["deploy"])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `gid` (Number) Numeric group ID to look up. Conflicts with `name`. When looking up by `name`, the gid of the group that was found. If several groups share a gid, the first one in `/etc/group` is returned.
- `name` (String) Group name to look up. Conflicts with `gid`. When looking up by `gid`, the name of the group that was found.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data source identifier (equal to `name`).
- `members` (Set of String) Usernames listed as members of the group in `/etc/group`. Users whose primary group this is are not included unless they are also listed explicitly.

## Errors

| Situation | Diagnostic |
|-----------|------------|
| Both or neither of `name` and `gid` are set | `Invalid Attribute Combination` |
| No group with that name or gid exists in `/etc/group` | `Group not found` |
| `/etc/group` cannot be read or contains a malformed line | `Reading group database` |

## Caveats

- To list several groups, for example all groups in a gid range or all groups a user is a member of, use the [`sysutils_groups`](./groups.md) data source.
- `members` lists only the users named in the group's `/etc/group` entry. Users whose primary group this is are members too, but are not listed there; look them up with the [`sysutils_user`](./user.md) data source and compare its `gid`.
- The data source only works on Unix-like systems.
